articles.title: Poland arrests four over alleged spying for Russia
articles.summary: Poland has charged four people with espionage and says they were spying for Moscow. Two more have been accused of shipping military components to Russia.

image.caption: Poland's Internal Security Agency, known as ABW, investigates espionage, terrorism and threats to national securityImage: Krzysztof Zatycki/ZUMA/picture alliance

blocks.text: Polish authorities said Thursday they had arrested six people over alleged military component shipments to Russia, four of whom they charged with espionage.
Investigators said the group illegally supplied Moscow with significant quantities of parts used to manufacture ammunition and weapons systems despite an embargo.
What are the suspects accused of?

Four suspects, including the Russian woman, were charged with espionage and placed in pretrial detention for three months, Poland's Internal Security Agency (ABW) said. The other two are subject to non-custodial restrictions.
All six also face allegations of violating rules governing international trade in goods and technologies of strategic importance to national defense and international security.
"Russia is subject to a strict embargo in this area, and this operation was designed to circumvent it," Siemoniak told reporters.
The suspects are five Poles aged 25 to 52 and a 37-year-old Russian woman, intelligence coordinator Tomasz Siemoniak said.
Why is Poland concerned about Russian operations?
Poland, an EU and NATO member, is a major supporter of Ukraine and the main transit route for Western military and humanitarian aid to the country.
Siemoniak said nearly 100 people had been charged in ABW espionage and sabotage investigations since January 1, 2024.

Warsaw has repeatedly accused Russia of sabotage since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. On Tuesday, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Poland had foiled a possible provocation at its border with Russia's Kaliningrad exclave.
The Russian Embassy did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The Kremlin has consistently denied conducting sabotage operations in NATO countries.

articles.title: NUP House members willing to disclose their amendments in proposed 2027 budget
articles.summary: House NUP members are willing to disclose the budget amendments they included in the proposed P7.2 trillion budget for 2027, Deputy =Speaker Ronaldo Puno of Antipolo said Thursday.

blocks.text: Published November 5, 2026 6:38pm

Members of the National Unity Party (NUP) in the House of Representatives are willing to disclose the budget amendments they included in the proposed P7.2 trillion budget for 2027, Deputy Speaker Ronaldo Puno of Antipolo said Thursday.

Puno made the announcement after the NUP’s dialogue with the People’s Budget Coalition, which earlier flagged House amendments for the 2027 budget for supposed lack of documentation and stamp of approval by the concerned government agency.
“We fully support disclosure [of budget amendments]. In fact, today, I made a disclosure and explanation to the People's Budget Coalition on projects on my district,” Puno said in a press conference.
“I have informed them that any congressman in the National Unity Party is willing to provide them with such details. And we think anybody in Congress has the obligation to do this,” Puno added.
Puno said NUP is willing to show the trail from where the project proposal originated until it was included in the House-approved version.

“In fact, we went a little bit beyond that, that it must follow the bottom-up budget approach. Meaning to say, it has to begin with the barangay, go to the local government, eventually go to the Regional Development Council, then it goes to the agency. There's no reason why these things will not be documented,” Puno said.

Likewise, Puno said that the NUP will push for the inclusion of a special provision which will allow the Department of Agriculture (DA) to location of eight farm to market roads that it proposed to Congress with wrong coordinates.

Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian earlier said that the Senate will remove P8 billion worth of projects included in the proposed budget of the Department of Public Works and Highways due to lack of documentation.
Sought for comment on this action, Puno supported Gatchalian’s position.
“We believe that if it has no documentation, it has no right to be there [in the budget],” Puno said.
“We know the Senate is planning to eliminate them, [and] we will not object,” Puno added.

House appropriations panel senior vice chairperson Abet Garcia of Bataan, for his part, said that amendments introduced by lawmakers in the national budget are made based on requests from many sectors which are not easy to balance.

“The requests [for Congress to increase their budget on certain projects and items], they do not only come from government agencies. There are also requests from local government units. These requests are the ones that us members of the House try to address to balance the need to fund the needs of the people in a local and national level scale,” Garcia said.

“So, with limited resources, it's really a balancing act. And during the budget hearings, we learn about the absorptive capacity of implementing agencies, and which projects should be prioritized, to come up with a final version of the House General Appropriations Bill. And if I may say, in the end, wala pong masaya kasi limited yung budget, but we have to come up with a workable budget,” Garcia added.
(Nobody really ends up happy because of limited resources.) — BM, GMA News

articles.title: Who are the Cabinet members of BARMM chief Macacua’s admin?
articles.summary: The newly constituted Cabinet brings a mix of veteran lawmakers, technocrats, and legal professionals to lead the region's ministries and offices

blocks.text: CABINET. BARMM Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua announces on November 5, 2026 the newly constituted Cabinet of his administration, marking what he hailed as a "defining moment" in Bangsamoro history.
BARMM FB live/Screenshot
The newly constituted Cabinet brings a mix of veteran lawmakers, technocrats, and legal professionals to lead the region's ministries and offices

COTABATO CITY, Philippines – Following the historic inauguration of the region’s first-ever elected parliament, Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua officially announced on Thursday, November 5 the newly constituted Cabinet of his administration, marking what he hailed as a “defining moment” in Bangsamoro history.

The announcement comes on the heels of a vetting and screening process conducted by a special committee, designed to select leaders based on “competence, professional experience, integrity, and a strict commitment to moral governance.”
“To my fellow Bangsamoro, this government is yours,” Macacua declared. “We will pursue a policy of moral governance, integrity, and accountability.”

blocks.text: Macacua acknowledged that the governance workload ahead is immense, but emphasized that the regional leadership’s resolve remains even greater. He underscored the administration’s dedication to preserving the hard-won gains of the peace process.

“We commit to sustaining the gains of the peace process and ensuring that the dividends of autonomy are felt in every household and every community,” Macacua said. “Together, with the continued support of our national government, local government units, and our partners, we will write a new chapter of peace, prosperity, and dignity for our people.”

Reflecting on the big tasks ahead, Macacua underscored that the newly formed administration will vigorously pursue moral governance—the foundational policy initiated by former chief minister Al Haj Murad Ebrahim.

“My fellow Bangsamoro, this government is yours,” Macacua stated. “We will pursue and vanish your moral or moral governance that had been initiated by former chief minister Al Haj Murad Ebrahim. Indeed, the work ahead is immense, but our resolve is greater.”
Macacua also committed his administration to sustaining the ongoing peace process and ensuring that the tangible dividends of regional autonomy reach every household and community.

He also expressed gratitude for the continued, collaborative backing of the national government, inter-governmental units, and international and local partners in cultivating peace, prosperity, and dignity for the Bangsamoro land and its people. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Finland court jails captain and crew member over Baltic cable sabotage
articles.summary: Finland seized the Fitburg freighter last year over the suspected sabotage of cables linking Helsinki and Tallinn. It's one of several incidents of damaged infrastructure in the Baltic since Russia's…

image.caption: The Fitburg was en route to Israel when it was seized by Finnish authorities in the Baltic Sea for alleged sabotageImage: Finnish Police/Handout/REUTERS

blocks.text: A Finnish court on Thursday convicted the Russian captain and a senior crew member of the cargo ship Fitburg for damaging two undersea telecommunications cables in the Gulf of Finland last year.
The Helsinki District Court found the two defendants guilty of "aggravated criminal damage."
It said in a statement that they had intentionally dragged the ship's anchor along the seabed for around 130 kilometers (81 miles).
The captain was sentenced to three and a half years in jail, while the crew member, an Azerbaijani citizen, was sentenced to two years and 10 months.
They were also ordered to jointly pay around €1.9 million ($2.1 million) in damages, the Reuters news agency reported, with the captain to pay about €85,000 more.
The defendants denied any wrongdoing and have challenged Finland's jurisdiction in the case.
What else do we know about the Fitburg freighter?
Finnish authorities seized the vessel on December 31 on suspicion that it had damaged cables linking Finland's capital, Helsinki, and Tallinn, Estonia.
Finnish police at the time said the ship had been dragging its anchor for hours when it was discovered.
The Fitburg and its 14-member crew had been en route to the port of Haifa, Israel, from the Russian city of St. Petersburg when the incident occurred.

Finland has stepped up efforts to protect its undersea infrastructure following a series of incidents involving cables and pipelines in the Baltic Sea since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

articles.title: 'Big chance' of Bato dela Rosa getting arrested, says NBI's Matibag
articles.summary: National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag on Thursday expressed belief that there is a big possibility that embattled Senator Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa will be located and arrested…

blocks.text: Published November 5, 2026 6:27pm

National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag on Thursday expressed belief that there is a big possibility that embattled Senator Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa will be located and arrested soon.
In an ambush interview, Matibag said authorities may start conducting operations, based on intelligence reports, to determine Dela Rosa's exact whereabouts.
"Baka any time soon we'll have some operations just to eliminate 'yung areas that we've identified based on the intel reports that we're having," the NBI chief said.
(Maybe any time soon we'll have some operations just to eliminate the areas that we've identified based on the intel reports that we're having.)
"I think with the information that we're getting, baka malaki 'yung tsansa (there might be a big chance)," he added.
Asked if Dela Rosa is hiding in Mindanao, Matibag said he could not tell for sure.
"Basta we have strong belief na nandito siya sa Pilipinas. But though, that's a possibility," he said.
(We just have a strong belief that he is here in the Philippines. But though, that's a possibility.)

Dela Rosa has been issued an arrest warrant from the International Criminal Court (ICC) in relation to the drug war of former president Rodrigo Duterte. The senator was chief of the Philippine National Police (PNP) at the time the war on drugs was implemented.

The Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) has raised a P50-million reward for the arrest of Dela Rosa, who according to Interior Secretary Juanito Victor "Jonvic" Remulla is considered "armed and dangerous."
Remulla also said authorities were also negotiating with a group protecting the senator to secure his surrender and prevent a potentially violent confrontation.
Duterte, meanwhile, is detained at the ICC in The Hague, Netherlands, while awaiting his crimes against humanity trial this month. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: France gears up for strikes and protests as unions promise national mobilisation
articles.summary: Five of France's unions have joined a wave of strikes and protests in a national day of action.

blocks.text: Hundreds of thousands of demonstrators are expected to take part in marches across France as five unions join strikes and protests in a national day of action.
The protests began in September with high school students complaining about poor conditions and resources in education, but have spread to include the so-called "yellow-vest" movement and workers.
Authorities expect 500,000 to 700,000 demonstrators to join marches, with tens of thousands more in Paris alone, in a day billed by one union leader as "a great day of convergence".
The five unions have combined forces across the public and private sector, with demands for higher wages to combat the cost of living and protected public services.
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez has said that 70,000 police and gendarmes are being deployed, vowing "an extremely firm response" to any potential outbreaks of violence.
More than 250 separate actions are planned for 5 November, with some disruption reported in schools, hospitals and public transport.
Workers have also been asked to halt production at oil refineries, and France is expected to import more electricity than it produces on Thursday because of disruption at nuclear plants.

A coalition of unions has urged workers, pensioners and young people to join Thursday's day of strikes to intensify pressure on the government. In particular they are seeking a rise in the minimum wage, or Smic, which is currently €12.31 (£10) an hour.
The head of the CFDT union, Marylise Léon, complained that it was not just the minimum wage that needed to increase: "We are asking for a net increase of €100 a month."

The government has sought to appease public anger over rising prices, bringing down the cost of fuel by releasing 10 million barrels of diesel from strategic reserves. Ministers have also promised school students to reform the unpopular Parcoursup university admissions platform and eventually replace it by 2028.

Some 81 lycées - high schools that cater for 15-18 year-olds - were shut on Thursday morning, according to the education ministry. It added that about 17.5% of primary schools too were affected by the strikes.
Large numbers are expected on the streets, especially in the capital, and Léon said she would be happy if 800,000 people turned out.
One union leader Sophie Binet, who called it the "great day of convergence", added: "The time has come to take the mobilisation to the next level; the strike must take over."

Meanwhile, a revived gilets jaunes (yellow-vest) movement that staged a revolt against the high cost of living several years ago has called for further blockades and protests on Friday and Saturday too.

articles.title: Who’s next for Maharlika Fund after Joel Consing?
articles.summary: 'Whatever we have achieved can only grow from here,' says Maharlika Investment Corporation's top boss, Joel Consing, who's set to step down on November 23

blocks.text: PCEO. Maharlika Investment Corporation President and CEO Joel Consing speaks to the media on Thursday, November 5.
Lance Spencer Yu/Rappler
'Whatever we have achieved can only grow from here,' says Maharlika Investment Corporation's top boss, Joel Consing, who's set to step down on November 23

items: Rafael 'Joel' Consing Jr. will conclude his term as head of the Maharlika Investment Corporation on November 23, with no confirmed successor announced.
Consing plans to leave behind extensive research and documentation for his successor, emphasizing the importance of institutional culture and continuity within the organization.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
Rafael “Joel” Consing Jr. knows exactly when his time at the Maharlika Investment Corporation (MIC) ends.
November 23. Five o’clock sharp.
But who will take over the country’s still-young sovereign wealth fund? That part we don’t yet know.
“It’s been reported my term as PCO ends at the end of this month. Any announcement on the transition will come from the Palace,” Consing told reporters on Thursday, November 5.

blocks.caption: Who’s next for Maharlika Fund after Joel Consing?

blocks.text: Leaving too is MIC’s chief investment and operating officer Kheed Nielsen Ng, who is co-terminus with Consing.

Though MIC’s boss has kept mum on who might take his place, one name making the rounds is Finance Undersecretary Ma. Angela “Angel” Ignacio, who oversees the Department of Finance’s (DOF) Government Corporations and Investments Group.

Ignacio joined the DOF in February 2026, but she is no stranger to Finance Secretary Frederick Go or Consing himself. All three previously worked at the now-defunct Office of the Special Assistant to the President for Investment and Economic Affairs, which Go headed before taking over the DOF. Ignacio served as an undersecretary, while Consing was its executive director before taking the helm at Maharlika.
When asked about it, Consing offered no confirmation. The appointment, he said, remains the call of the President.
So after three years at the helm, does Consing have any parting instructions?
“I don’t give instructions to my successors,” Consing said. “No instructions, just a suggested path forward.”

What he is leaving behind, however, is paperwork. Lots of it. MIC departments are assembling year-end reports. For his part, Consing is preparing a compendium of his research papers, which he intends to share with his successor and the Land Bank of the Philippines.
“All the stuff that we’re doing actually came as a result of my research background. And I’ve written much more than what we’ve done. I’m turning over all of those to my successor,” he said.

There is also the matter of preserving the institutional culture, arguably just as important a matter, especially for a fledgling sovereign wealth fund that found its inception marred by governance concerns.

“One of the messages that I’ve always told them, and I continue to tell them, and which I will tell them on the 23rd when I leave is: They are the legacy of MIC, apart from what it aims to achieve. And they’re also my continuation, my transition. So hence, whatever we have achieved can only grow from here,” he said.
As for his own next act, Consing said he is leaving government, though he did not rule out returning someday.
Before joining the government in 2023, he was the chief financial officer of Enrique Razon Jr.’s International Container Terminal Services Inc. and managing director at HSBC.
For now, he says he is occupied with making sure MIC is left “very, very strong” and with handing over a “very healthy organization” to his successor. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Several European flights receive bomb threats, some divert
articles.summary: Several flights across Europe have either diverted or landed with a military escort after bomb or security threats. The first reported case involved a flight from Dublin to Rome landing outside…

image.caption: The Evreux airbase in northeastern France, not far from Paris, is typically used for military purposes not commercial flights [FILE: July 9, 2025]Image: JP Pariente/SIPA/picture alliance

blocks.text: Several commercial flights made either unscheduled or high-alert landings in France, Italy, Belgium and Bulgaria, according to authorities in the various countries.

Planes made unscheduled landings in Evreux, France; and in Bulgaria. A flight from Finland landed in Rome as scheduled but with a military escort, and another landed in Brussels amid a security threat.
The incident in France became public knowledge first, but the other similar reports soon followed.
This follows bomb threats leveled against several European flights earlier this week, prompting a series of similar unscheduled landings.
What do we know about the first incident outside Paris?
An Airbus A320 plane has been diverted to the Evreux airbase to the west of Paris following a bomb threat.
The office of French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu announced the incident on Thursday, saying it was monitoring the situation "in real time."
The flight was headed from Dublin, Ireland, to the Italian capital of Rome.
Tracking websites showed the plane, part of the Aer Lingus fleet, sharply deviating its course as it was around Paris' airspace and heading towards the more isolated airfield in Evreux.
France's air force said that it dispatched planes "as soon as the incident was reported."
"The aircraft has been diverted and is being escorted to Evreux airfield," it said.
Lecornu's office subsequently confirmed that the plane, part of the Aer Lingus fleet, had landed safely at the airfield.
What happened during the earlier disruptions?
The prior threats to commercial flights this week turned out to be hoaxes that nevertheless caused diversions and major security mobilizations.
In one case, the Italian air force escorted a plane to its emergency landing.
The threats targeted airlines including Poland's LOT, Scandinavian Airlines, Wizz Air and Ryanair.

While it's not yet clear if there is a link, these disruptions to commercial aviation also coincided with a series of apparent cyberattacks targeting freezer units in major supermarkets and even French bloodbanks.
All the cases remain nascent, but have the potential hallmarks of so-called hybrid attacks designed to cause maximum disruption with minimal effort and resources.
This is a developing story, more to follow.

articles.title: 2 tagged in Bacoor pet crematorium case surrender to NBI; charges to be filed
articles.summary: The husband and wife allegedly responsible for the dumped pet remains in Bulacan have surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), according to Director Melvin Matibag on Thursday.

blocks.text: Published November 5, 2026 6:09pm
The husband and wife allegedly responsible for the dumped pet remains in Bulacan have surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), according to Director Melvin Matibag on Thursday.
Matibag thanked the NBI Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) for cracking the case, calling it a “major breakthrough”.

“Nakuha kaagad natin yung person responsible dun sa pagbabaon nung mga pets na supposed to be na-cremate. Dalawa yung individual natin na subject ngayon, which is under our custody, voluntarily na pumunta dito sa atin at nakuhanan natin yung story kung paano ito nangyari and we will be filing the necessary charges dito sa mga individuals na ito,” Matibag said in a press conference.

(We got the person responsible for burying these pets that were supposed to be cremated. Two of the individuals that are under our custody voluntarily went here and we got the story on how this happened and we will be filing the necessary charges against these individuals.)
According to Matibag, the couple who owns the Ahjay Paws Aftercare Pet Crematorium in Bacoor, Cavite also owned a crematorium in San Jose Del Monte, Bulacan.
The pets in Bacoor were being sent to San Jose Del Monte for cremation, and then the ashes were supposed to be returned.

“Ang findings na natin dito, Ahjay Paws Aftercare Pet Crematorium, wala siyang facility, wala siyang equipment to do the cremation. So pinadala niya doon. Malaki yung volume ng dumarating,” Matibag said.

(Our findings here: Ahjay Paws Aftercare Pet Crematorium, they do not have the facility; they do not have the equipment to do the cremation. So they were brought there. There was a large volume being brought there.)
“So ang ginawa nila, linibing nila,” he added, citing the couple’s testimony. (So what they did, they buried them.)

Matibag said that the lack of proper cremation facilities points to evidence of estafa, as well as violations of the Consumer Protection Act. The NBI is also determining if there were violations in health and sanitation standards over the transferring of the dead pets from Bacoor to San Jose Del Monte.
The NBI has pinpointed three dumpsites, Matibag said.
When no more ashes were being returned to the Bacoor crematorium, the crematorium itself came up with ashes. Matibag said that no cremation took place at all.

Matibag said that the NBI will file six cases initially, since there were six complainants who came forward to the agency. However, Matibag said that there was already enough evidence for them to also file a case before the prosecutor’s office.
A large portion of the case has already been solved, Matibag said. He urged any other possible complainants to come forward, since there was already plenty of evidence.

However, Matibag said that they were also determining the liability of other parties, especially since the Bacoor pet crematorium was able to operate for so long even if they did not have the proper facilities.
The NBI is also attempting to get an Immigration Lookout Bulletin Order for other people who may be involved in the case, so that they will not escape, according to Matibag. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: [Rappler Investigates] Who’s taking care of our dead?
articles.summary: How could the living get through their own painful experience of saying their final goodbyes if embalmers weren’t there to help preserve the memory of their loved ones?

blocks.text: Many of us finished paying homage to our beloved departed in the past weekend or so, offering prayers and remembering them in very special ways.

There might have been different circumstances of their passing and varying means of sending them to their final resting place. But one common thing they must have all undergone was dignified preparation of their remains for grieving family members left behind to bid them tearful, sometimes painful, farewells.
This is made possible only by the careful handling of their bodies by embalmers, who are often faceless individuals because they remain behind the scenes in mortuaries.

Researcher Eirene Manatlao partnered with Henry Luce Foundation scholar Jake Gomez to take a peek into the little known world of embalmers — often stereotyped as uneducated or unclean because they handle the dead.

Jake discovered that embalmers need a “high school diploma, at least 140 hours of instruction from an accredited institution, and proof that they have embalmed at least 10 cadavers within a year.” After about two months of classroom instruction, they spend another month working on real cadavers in funeral homes.
They are required to pass an exam to obtain a license that must be renewed every three years.

In 2018, there were an estimated 5,000 licensed embalmers on record in the country but the number may not be as accurate. Today, very rough estimates put the count at a little over 6,000. Depending on employers, they get benefits and privileges on top of minimum wage. Others get paid by the number of bodies they handle, charging about P1,000 per body.
Eirene spoke to two embalmers and found a common vulnerability — processing the remains of babies that made them cry because they, too, are parents.

They’ve had to contend with the stigma associated with the profession and with common misperceptions. Their work requires attention to detail, taking as long as four hours per cadaver, sometimes longer, depending on the body’s physical condition.
One of them, Joycel Regalado, pointed out the importance of what they do: “Kung wala kami, sino ang mag-aayos ng patay?” (If we weren’t here, who would take care of the dead?)
Very true, for how could the living get through their own painful experience of saying their final goodbyes if embalmers weren’t there to help preserve the memory of their loved ones?

Meanwhile, we, who are still here, are reminded to continue with the business and concerns of living: how to better cope with the looming Super El Niño and its effects on farmers, as well as the persisting energy crisis that has caused electricity bills to soar. We will be doing more stories on this extreme weather event that is threatening to break records and last through early next year.

The Visayas is expected to be problematic even if more than half of the Visayas grid’s power generation mix comes from renewable energy sources. Reporter John Sitchon, who is based in Cebu, warns that multiple red alerts are expected in the region in 2027 due to rising demand and unstable energy supply. He mapped the Visayas energy mix across the region’s five island sub-grids in Cebu, Bohol, Panay, Negros, and Leyet-Samar. Take a look here.

Researcher Shay Du looked into the affordability of going solar for household rooftops as a way of coping with mounting electricity bills. Estimated costs of putting up such solar panels range from P80,000 to P200,000 for average households, up to over half a million pesos for larger houses.

There are financing options available, according to Shay. Government employees considering going solar can take out loans from the Government Service Insurance System, while private employees can expect loans from the Social Security System by 2027. Home improvement loans via Pag-IBIG are also available.

Let’s not lose sight of other big issues that might get past us because of more urgent daily living concerns. Let’s continue monitoring how public funds are being allocated and who will be chosen by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. as new members of the Supreme Court, including his pick as replacement of Chief Justice Gesmundo, who retires this Friday, November 6.
Till Thursday after next!

articles.title: Rizal farmer loses home to floods, raises questions about quarrying, waste management
articles.summary: This farmer in Rodriguez, Rizal, lost her home and crops to floodwater, mud, and waste in 2024. She still raises concerns about quarry traffic, children’s safety, and waste management.

blocks.text: RIZAL, Philippines – At around 4 pm on August 31, 2024, “Ditoy” (her name changed to protect her privacy) was alone inside her home in Sitio Laan, Barangay Macabud, in Rodriguez, Rizal, when floodwater, mud, and rubbish buried the house. She tried to leave, but the door had jammed, possibly swollen by the rain.

“Baha, putik, ‘tsaka basura ang magkasama noon,” she said. “Andiyan na ‘yung tubig na napakaitim, napakabaho ng amoy.” (It was a mix of floodwater, mud, and trash. The water was pitch-black and foul-smelling.)

Ditoy’s family lost their home and the crops that helped feed them and bring in small amounts of money. More than two years later, she continues to seek answers about waste disposal and quarry activity near Sitio Laan.
Ditoy attributed the rubbish to illegal dumping near Sitio Pintor in San Isidro, Rodriguez. She alleged that people dumped waste outside the sanitary landfill to avoid paying disposal fees.

On November 2, 2024, the municipality declared businessman Wennie Destacamento, owner of Survivor Hauling Services and 5WRD Hauling Services, persona non grata through Resolution No. 95, series of 2024.

Citing reports from the Municipal Environment and Natural Resources Office and a request from Mayor Ronnie Evangelista, the resolution addressed reports of illegal dumping along MWSS Road in Sitio Matang Tubig, Barangay San Jose, and parts of Sitio Pintor, Barangay San Isidro, as well as a garbage landslide in Sitio Laan, Barangay Macabud.
The municipality’s allegations, however, do not yet establish a court finding of liability.

Waste management in Rodriguez has faced scrutiny. In February 2026, a collapse at the Rodriguez sanitary landfill prompted an emergency response. The Department of Environment and Natural Resources ordered a halt to operations in part of the facility, citing operational and safety concerns, including erosion in the active waste-disposal area and a risk of further collapse.

The incident also drew broader concerns about the effects of landfill and quarry operations on nearby communities. Commenters on a Facebook post by the Philippine Red Cross Rizal Chapter about its response to the incident raised issues affecting residents beyond the immediate emergency.

The Rizal provincial government denied responsibility for the incident, saying the facility was privately operated. It is reported that International Solid Waste Integrated Management Specialist Inc. (ISWIMS) operated the Rodriguez facility through Green Leap Solid Waste Management Inc.

The collapse occurred nearly 18 months after Ditoy’s home was buried. It does not establish where the waste that reached her property came from, but it shows the continuing questions surrounding waste disposal and the safety of communities near landfill operations.

Her family had completed a P20,000 payment in February 2024 for what they understood to be rights to the land. They built a home there, hoping to give their children a place to grow up. The disaster destroyed the house and crops that helped feed the family and brought in small amounts of money.

Ditoy sometimes asked her child to sell sweet potato leaves and taro shoots to a teacher to help pay for school expenses. Her husband also collects recyclable materials at a sanitary landfill to support the household.
When the house was swept away, years of savings and hard work seemed to vanish.

“Diyos ko po, nung natangay ‘yung bahay namin, parang lahat ng problema sumaklob! Back to zero!” she said. (When our house was swept away, my God, it felt like every problem descended upon us all at once. Back to zero!)
Afterward, barangay officials helped the family find another place to stay and provided a written agreement, she said. The family has since begun planting again.
Ditoy’s concerns extend beyond waste disposal. She said heavy trucks associated with quarry operations pass beside homes in Sitio Laan, keeping residents awake with their horns and rumbling engines.

“Puro dump truck po doon, sobrang daming dump truck. Daan sa gilid ng mga bahay, ‘di na makatulog sa gabi,” she said. (There are so many dump trucks there. They pass alongside the houses, making it difficult [for residents] to sleep at night.)
Ditoy identified “ATN” as one of the quarry operations in the area.

Public records confirm that ATN Holdings Inc. operates the ATN Integrated Aggregates Project, a quarrying and rock-crushing facility in Barangay Macabud, Rodriguez. The firm was among 11 quarry and crushing-plant operators whose permits the DENR suspended in December 2020 following Typhoon Ulysses. Its mineral-processing permit was reinstated in January 2021. (READ: What went wrong during Typhoon Ulysses?)
Ditoy recalled an incident in which a dump truck crushed a sidecar. The driver managed to jump clear, she said.
“Eh, paano kung may angkas ‘yun? May sakay na pamilya?” she asked. (What if there had been a passenger? What if a family had been on board?)

She also worries about dust from quarry operations and its possible effects on children. She said children in the community often become sick when it rains and described dust and dirt entering homes through gaps in their walls.

She said nearby streams had also changed: one that was once narrow had widened, while another that used to be deep had become shallower as sand accumulated. She fears that water held near a quarry could rush toward homes below if the land retaining it gives way.

Richard Ybañez, a licensed geologist and chief science research specialist at the University of the Philippines Resilience Institute, said quarrying can alter hills and waterways, affecting how runoff moves through a watershed. Excavations may also retain water, depending on the terrain and drainage.

Establishing quarrying’s contribution to a particular flood, Ybañez said, requires comparable data from before and after landscape changes, including information on topography, vegetation, rainfall and urban development.
“The data has to be there before and after,” he told Rappler.

His comments do not settle the causes of the flooding or the changes Ditoy described. They point to the evidence needed to assess those concerns, which residents say affect their homes and daily lives.

Government action on quarrying in Rizal dates back decades. In 1998, the DENR temporarily suspended quarrying and crushing operations in Rodriguez and San Mateo amid concerns about flooding, erosion and siltation. A 1999 DENR order permanently prohibited mining and quarrying within the Marikina Watershed Reservation, but did not ban all quarrying across Rizal.

After Typhoon Ulysses in 2020, the government again suspended quarry and crushing-plant permits in the Marikina River Basin while investigating possible links to flooding. The Mines and Geosciences Bureau’s subsequent assessment found quarrying made a “minimal” contribution to flooding and siltation in the Marikina River during that event. It identified heavy rainfall, urbanization, erosion, deforestation and other land disturbances as contributing factors.
The debate continues in the 20th Congress. House Bill No. 4313, filed in September 2025 by Rizal 1st District Representative Rebecca Maria “Mia” Ynares, seeks to declare Rizal a mining-free zone.

As of October 2026, the bill remained pending with the committee on natural resources. The lawmaker has yet to respond to an interview request about the proposal’s implementation, enforcement and treatment of existing operations.
Ditoy said she had not known about the bill before. Initially, she said change might still be possible. Then she reconsidered.
“Pero parang hindi na,” she said. (But it seems that’s no longer the case.)
She questioned whether improvements would last if residents continued receiving short-term assistance without long-term solutions.

“Parang masusolusyunan nang panandalian, pero hindi pangmatagalan,” she said. “Puro na lang ayuda-ayuda, wala nang solusyon na pangmatagalan.” (It might be resolved temporarily, but not in the long term. It is always just aid, with no lasting solutions.)

Ditoy helps lead the Sitio Laan Ladies Association, a group of women organizing to raise community concerns. For her, the issue goes beyond rebuilding a home. She wants officials to pay attention to the conditions residents face every day, particularly those affecting children.
“Sana po bigyang-pansin din po ng gobyerno ‘yung lugar namin,” she said. (I hope the government will also pay attention to our area.) – Rappler.com
Dominique Astucia is a Rappler intern studying BA Journalism at the University of Santo Tomas.

articles.title: ‘Everybody’s pissed’: Sand blowing into homes next to rural N.S. subdivision development
articles.summary: Residents say they're fed up with blowing sand from the site of a subdivision development in the middle of a quiet neighbourhood in Coldbrook, N.S.

image.caption: A large sandpit has formed in a Coldbrook, N.S., neighbourhood as the result of a subdivision development. Nearby residents say sand is blowing everywhere, including inside their homes. (Jeorge Sadi/CBC)

blocks.text: Nova Scotia·New
Residents say they're fed up with blowing sand from the site of a subdivision development in the middle of a quiet neighbourhood in Coldbrook, N.S.
Municipal and provincial governments say nothing wrong with 14-hectare sandpit
When Jill Alcoe-Holland lifted the cover off her backyard pool in Coldbrook, N.S., earlier this year, she discovered so much muck that she immediately sent down her robotic pool cleaner.
It had its work cut out.
“For 15 days, every few hours, I was pulling up a robot full of sand,” she said.

The sand came from a 14-hectare sandpit in the middle of the quiet Annapolis Valley neighbourhood that will eventually be the site of a 30-home subdivision. The sand was dug up and is being shipped out in large dump trucks at all hours of the day, according to residents.
Sand blowing from the pit is going through their windows, covering their parked vehicles and front steps and, when it’s very windy, forcing them to leave their backyards and go inside, they say.
A robotic pool cleaner is filled with mud after operating in a pool in the backyard of a home in Coldbrook, N.S. (Submitted by Jill Alcoe-Holland)
Alcoe-Holland said her family made the mistake of opening all their windows and doors on one of the first warm days of the year.
“We came in for supper and we could write our name on our kitchen table because it was covered with sand,” Alcoe-Holland said.
'Basically a sandstorm'
More than 60 residents in the neighbourhood have signed a petition calling on government officials to do something to mitigate the blowing sand and ensure the subdivision is built sooner than later.
The residents say they aren’t opposed to the new subdivision, but they cannot tolerate having sand everywhere anymore.
“Everybody’s kind of pissed off,” said Rick Young, whose home is directly next to the sandpit.
Why this massive sandpit has neighbours 'pissed off'
Young said he and his wife can’t open the upstairs windows in their house without sand getting in.
He said he’s found sand built up on the windshields of their vehicles parked in the driveway.
“You didn't dare turn your windshield wipers on. You're scared you’ll scratch your windshield. There was that much sand,” Young said.
The front steps of Rick Young's home, which is right next to the sandpit, are covered in sand that's blown over from the subdivision development. (Rick Young)
David Grant also has to keep his windows closed at times because of the piles of sand that tower over the trees in his backyard.
He was doing yardwork this summer when the wind picked up and made him run for cover, he said.
“There was basically a sandstorm,” he said. “It was bad enough that it was bothering my breathing and I had to go inside.”
Grant said he and his wife have been considering selling their home, but they don’t know how long the sandpit will be here and believe it could reduce their property’s value.
No rules being broken
Subdivision development permits are the responsibility of municipal governments and open pits are regulated by the province.
But pits made as a result of subdivision development don’t need permits, according to a spokesperson for the Department of Environment and Climate Change.
Department staff have visited the site several times and the work is compliant with provincial regulations, the spokesperson said in an email.
Residents are also upset about large dump trucks carrying sand out of the neighbourhood at all hours of the day. (Jeorge Sadi/CBC)

A site development manager with Lutz Trucking Ltd., which is the company doing the work, declined an interview request but said they’re taking all precautions and have met with residents to try to address their concerns.
“It is enormous. There's no question. That was my first impression,” said Dave Corkum, mayor of the Municipality of Kings County.
Corkum said he has heard from several residents about the pit and understands their frustrations.
Despite its size, he said the municipality can’t do anything about it, but he believes the province can do more.
Large piles of sand can be seen through the trees in David Grant's backyard. (Jeorge Sadi/CBC)
“There certainly should be regulations and rules involved when you're right in the middle of a large-scale subdivision,” Corkum said.
There is a two-year time limit for developing a subdivision in Kings County but there can be delays, according to the mayor.
The sandpit has already been there for a year. Residents are afraid they’ll be living next to it for many more months before a subdivision is finished.
“It certainly doesn't look like it's going to happen in the near future,” said Grant, as he waits to sell his home.

articles.title: PSA finds evidence of Joseph Sy's 'fake' records
articles.summary: The Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) said Thursday it found evidence showing that embattled businessman Joseph Sy procured fake documents during his birth registration process.

blocks.text: The Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) said Thursday it found evidence showing that embattled businessman Joseph Sy procured fake documents during his birth registration process.

PSA Legal Service Director Atty. Eliezer Ambatali said this during the continuation of the Senate Committee on Justice and Human Rights’ hearing into the case of Sy---a nickel businessman who was previously arrested after his biometrics matched those of a Chinese citizen Chen Zhong Zhen.
Ambatali said the Office of the Solicitor General (OSG) has already filed a petition for the cancellation of the birth records of Sy.

“Doon sa investigation namin…investigation ng Fraud Management Division ito ng PSA, we found out that there is evidence that would say na merong…mga procurement ng fake documents during the registration,” Ambatali said.
(In our investigation, conducted by the PSA’s Fraud Management Division, we discovered evidence indicating that fake documents were procured during Sy’s registration process.)

“This type of fraud is the second type. It happens at the source, during the registration. So these are fake ‘yung baptismal certificate…hindi makita ‘yung birth records ng mga magulang, hindi rin namin makita ‘yung mga records ng hilot or ‘yung attending person during the time of birth,” he added.

(This type of fraud is the second type. It happens at the source, during the registration. For instance, we found that his baptismal certificates are fake; we cannot locate his parents’ birth records nor any records from his birth attendant or the person who assisted during his birth.)
Suspected of being a Chinese national parading as a Filipino, Sy was arrested by Philippine authorities in 2025 when he arrived at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport from Hong Kong.
But the Supreme Court (SC) First Division ordered last month the release of Sy, ruling in favor of his petition for habeas corpus.
The Bureau of Immigration (BI) said it respected the SC’s resolution on the petition, but clarified that the Court did not settle the matter of Sy’s nationality.
Fingerprints
Meanwhile, Bureau of Immigration (BI) Deputy Commissioner Atty. Joel Alejandro Nacnac also confirmed during the hearing that the fingerprints of Sy matched those of Chinese national Chen Zhong Zhen.
Committee chairperson Sen. Risa Hontiveros then asked when the fingerprints of Sy entered the BI database.
“Under our records, he is an applicant po ng returning resident visa way back in 1989. Subsequently, the permanent resident visa was approved in February of 1989,” Nacnac said.

“Later on, he also applied under RA 7919, it po ‘yung Alien Social Integration Program, which appears to be on record, March of 1996 na po. With this, ‘yung biometric records niya ay nakita at na-capture po ng Bureau,” he added.
(Later on, he also applied for the Alien Social Integration Program, which appears to be on record, March of 1996. With this, his biometric records were seen and captured by the Bureau.)
No show
Sy, who is the subject of the investigation, also failed to attend the hearing.
His lawyer, Alma Mallonga, said that the businessman called earlier this morning to say that he was in an emergency room of Makati Medical Center and “had been feeling unwell since last night.”

“Maybe part of it is the stress. The fact that he had been incarcerated for more than 491 days, Your Honor, and it’s just been less than three weeks since he was released,” Mallonga said, adding that her client also underwent certain “surgical procedures.”
Regardless, the lawyer said Sy had earlier expressed intent to attend the hearing.

Hontiveros, on the other hand, asked Sy’s lawyer to submit a medical certificate and instructed the committee secretary to coordinate with the Senate clinic to validate the condition of the embattled businessman.
The senator also said she is expecting that Sy will be attending the next committee hearing.
“Mr. Joseph Sy, inaasahan kita sa susunod na hearing. Kung kaya mo mag party-party, Baka kaya mo ring dumalo at harapin ang Senado ng Pilipinas,” Hontiveros said.
(Mr. Joseph Sy, I expect to see you at the next hearing. If you’re capable of partying, perhaps you’re also capable of attending and facing the Philippine Senate.) —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: South Korea tests Arctic shipping route amid Russia-West row
articles.summary: For South Korean ships, navigating off north coast of Russia dramatically reduces travel time to Europe, but the pro-Ukraine coalition might see it as undermining their efforts to isolate Moscow.

image.caption: Cargo ship PanStar Acro left from South Korean port hub of Busan in AugustImage: Jung Yeon-je/AFP

blocks.text: A South Korean container ship completed a voyage to Western Europe through the Arctic Ocean off the northern coast of Russia in October, fueling Seoul's hopes of exploiting the route as a shortcut for trade.

The ship made the round trip from Busan to Rotterdam in just 50 days, saving at least 10 days compared to the fastest travel times along the more commonly used Suez Canal route. The Northern Sea Route (NSR) is not only around 7,000 kilometers (4,350 miles) shorter, it also avoids the geopolitical flashpoint of the Middle East.
But the faster delivery times might not exactly trigger celebrations across western European capitals.

Analysts say the nations arrayed against Russia over its invasion of Ukraine fear that South Korean President Lee Jae-myung is looking to boost Seoul's economic relations with Moscow. This would run contrary to the efforts to cut off Russia made by Kyiv and its Western alies.

One of the reasons for South Korea testing the Arctic route is its undoubtedly large economic potential. But analysts told DW that Seoul also hopes that, by having a working relationship with the Russian regime, they could sway its leader Vladimir Putin against providing more weapons to North Korea.
Lee's government, they suggest, will need to navigate the geopolitical waters extremely carefully.
Climate change opening up NSR

The container vessel PanStar Acro left the South Korean port of Busan on August 22 and navigated around Russia to reach the southern UK port of Felixstowe, then continued its journey by sailing to Rotterdam in the Netherlands and Gdansk in Poland, before heading back along the NSR.

blocks.caption: PanStar Acro is not an ice breaker, but it has some ice-resistant design featuresImage: Yonhap News Agency/REUTERS

blocks.text: For decades, the NSR was impassable due to the North Pole ice cover. With the ice in retreat due to climate change, navigation is becoming possible, although commercial ships often need to be accompanied by an ice-breaker vessel at certain times of year.

According to the Arctic Council, an international body which includes the US, Russia, Canada, Norway, Sweden, Finland, Denmark and Iceland, last year saw a record 1,812 vessels operating in the Arctic. That marks an increase of 40% compared to 2013.

The NSR "presents significant economic potential" for South Korea by linking it more closely to the key markets of Europe while bypassing the challenging waters of the northwest Indian Ocean, said Joseph Kristanto, a maritime security analyst at Singapore's S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies.

"In addition to potentially lowering shipping costs and transit times, the route's development could strengthen Busan's position as a regional maritime hub and create opportunities for South Korea's shipbuilding sector," he told DW.
European Union unveils new Arctic strategy
The Lee government has outlined plans for regular commercial services on the NSR by 2030, with the first Korean ship to complete the voyage merely a test of the logistics.
Fears of 'strategic dependency'

The danger, however, is that by developing the NSR as South Korea's favored route to Europe, "it could introduce a new form of strategic dependency on Russia as Moscow exercises considerable control over navigation along its Arctic coastline," said Kristanto.
"From the European perspective, closer economic engagement with Russia risks undermining efforts to isolate Moscow over its invasion of Ukraine," he said.
Kristanto points out that Moscow could apply pressure through regulations and "the provision of icebreaker assistance.”

The analyst also said that European diplomats' concerns over Seoul's recent engagement with Moscow go beyond the NSR and include the alleged delivery of around 165,000 tons of fuel — aboard sanctioned Russian tankers — to Russia in August.
All of this is happening as Pyongyang, Seoul's archrival, is sending troops to help Russia in its war against Ukraine.
North Korea expands role in Russia's war with Ukraine
Was Seoul's row with Kyiv a calculated move?

"South Korea is very interested in accessing the NSR as climate change means that a route that was previously impossible to use is now accessible and makes perfect economic sense," said Andrei Lankov, a Russian-born professor of history and international relations at Seoul's Kookmin University.
At the same time, Seoul is "trying to send signals to the Russian government that it is willing to manage relations," Lankov said.

It also coincides with Seoul taking a firmer stance against Ukraine, a position that dates back to September, when President Volodymyr Zelenskyy addressed the UN General Assembly and confirmed that two North Koreans who had been taken prisoner in Ukraine had been moved to South Korea. Seoul reacted angrily and claimed that Zelenskyy had violated an agreement to keep the transfer of the two POWs secret.
Why Kyiv and Seoul are clashing over North Korean POWs
The dispute degenerated into a major diplomatic spat, with Seoul demanding apologies and ultimately withdrawing a number of its diplomats from Kyiv.

Lankov believes the row may have been somewhat performative on Seoul's part as it allowed Lee's administration to distance itself from Kyiv and resist pressure to provide material help to Ukraine. He said this stance would have been appreciated in Moscow.
"And then Russia could reciprocate by not providing North Korea with advanced and dangerous military technology," he added.
Korea keeps low profile while waiting for Ukraine war to end

"Right now, South Korea wants to fly under the radar, to examine the possibilities and be prepared for when the war is over, and sanctions on Russia are lifted in the future," said Lankov. "That's the economic plan, but they are also hoping that by working with Moscow they can halt the transfer of more weapons to the North."
Kristanto also expects Seoul to "pursue a cautious and incremental approach."

"Seoul is unlikely to abandon the initiative altogether, particularly given growing Chinese interest in Arctic shipping, but it will also seek to avoid unnecessarily antagonizing its Western partners," he said.

"Ultimately, South Korea is not necessarily choosing between Russia and the West, but attempting to preserve a potentially valuable economic opportunity without compromising its more fundamental strategic relationships," Kristanto added.

articles.title: Comelec targets 3 million new voters for 2028 elections
articles.summary: The Commission on Elections is aiming to add about three million voters to the rolls for the 2028 national and local elections when registration reopens nationwide on Tuesday, November 10.

blocks.text: November 5, 2026 | 5:36pm
Commission on Elections (Comelec) personnel insert official ballots into machines for verification at the National Printing Office (NPO) in Quezon City on January 15, 2025.
STAR / Miguel De Guzman

MANILA, Philippines — The Commission on Elections is aiming to add about three million voters to the rolls for the 2028 national and local elections when registration reopens nationwide on Tuesday, November 10.
The country currently has 71 million registered voters, Comelec Chairman George Erwin Garcia told reporters on Thursday, November 5.
If the poll body meets its target, that would bring the total number of voters to roughly 74 million for the highly anticipated May 2028 polls.
"We plan to register around three million voters," Garcia said in Filipino.
Registration will run until July 30, 2027.
The national and local elections are set for May 8, 2028, while the barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan elections are set for November 13 of the same year.
Garcia said the poll body moved the registration deadline up to July 30 from the originally planned September 30.
The earlier cutoff gives the commission time to confirm that those who file certificates of candidacy are registered voters in the places where they intend to run, Garcia said.
Registration will not open on November 10 in Naga City, Camarines Sur, or in Batanes, where voters go to the polls later this month.
Both areas will start accepting applications one week after their respective votes, Garcia said.
Naga will hold a plebiscite on November 21 to ratify its conversion into a highly urbanized city under Proclamation No. 1267, which President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. signed in May.
Batanes will hold a special election on November 28 to fill its lone congressional seat, left vacant after lawmaker Ciriaco Gato Jr. died in September.
No cedula, barangay certificates
Garcia also warned applicants that Comelec will no longer accept a barangay certification or a community tax certificate, commonly called a cedula, as proof of identity.
"In the past, these were always included, but this time we will not allow a barangay certification as proof of a registrant's identity," he said in Filipino.

Applicants should instead present a government-issued ID, Garcia said. He listed student IDs, library cards, police and National Bureau of Investigation clearances, and senior citizen IDs as acceptable alternatives.
Registration will run Tuesdays to Fridays at local election offices and at satellite and mall sites under Comelec's Register Anywhere Program.
Besides first-time applicants, the commission will process transfers, reactivations of deactivated records and corrections of entries.

articles.title: France braces for fresh protests as unions strike over higher wages
articles.summary: Unions representing the education sector, rail employees, public hospitals and postal services called the strike. Authorities have deployed some 70,000 police and security officers across the country.

image.caption: Riot police were deployed in Paris and other cities ahead of Thursday's protestsImage: Hannah McKay/REUTERS

blocks.text: Hundreds of thousands of people are expected to march in French cities on Thursday, as public workers go on strike alongside protesting students.

The mobilization, called by trade unions seeking higher wages, comes after demonstrations over education and the rising cost of living on October 17 triggered some of the worst rioting France has seen in years.
Police will be out in force for Thursday's protests, with Interior Minister Laurent Nunez announcing around 70,000 police officers and security forces would be deployed across the country.
Authorities estimate some 500,000 to 700,000 people will take part in the demonstrations, including about 80,000 in the capital, Paris.

blocks.caption: As part of Thursday's demonstrations, French high school students staged a sit-in in front of the Lycee Henri IV high school in ParisImage: Abdul Saboor/REUTERS

blocks.text: Who is striking on Thursday?
Public and private education unions have called for staff to walk off the job, as well as unions representing rail workers, public hospitals and postal services.
They are demanding for an increase in minimum wage, across-the-board wage raises, tax reforms and better learning conditions for young people.
The Education Ministry said 17.5% of ​primary school teachers were expected to strike. French power unions were also to join the action, state-owned utility EDF said.

Media reports said state railway operator SNCF expects only minor disruptions to long-distance services. It's not clear to what extent a strike called by air traffic controllers could disrupt air traffic.

blocks.caption: France has seen frequent nationwide protests over the cost of living in recent weeksImage: Christophe Archambault/AFP

blocks.text: Among those joining Thursday's marches are students who have been protesting for weeks over deteriorating learning conditions. Those demonstrations have grown to include widespread anger over high living costs and inequality.
Although the recent student-led protests have largely been peaceful, some saw clashes with police, with officers using tear gas and water cannons to disperse crowds, as well as rioting and looting.

blocks.text: Bomb squad in place to inspect plane with passengers, crew moved to safe place, France says
The French PM’s office has just confirmed the plane landed safely at Evreux with a bomb squad unit in place to inspect the aircraft.
151 passengers and six crew on board were moved to a safe place, it said.
Le Figaro is reporting the plane was escorted on approach by a French Rafale fighter jet.
BFMTV says the original bomb threat alert came from the Italian authorities.

blocks.caption: Jakub Krupa

blocks.text: Jakub Krupa
Earlier this week, seven planes across Europe were searched or diverted after a series of bomb threats were made to passenger flights.
The alarms affected flights operated by LOT Polish Airlines, SAS, WizzAir, and Ryanair.
Two of the flights also involved Rome Fiumicino airport, amid broader false bomb alarms in the country, which also affected 280 schools.
Flightradar24, one of the largest flight tracker websites in the world, also said that “no aircraft have departed from Rome Fiumicino Airport (FCO) in the past 30 minutes.”
The plane crossed the English Channel on a normal flight path to Rome before veering south-west of Paris and circling Chartres airport and diverting towards Évreux.
Curiously, in the last few minutes it flew right past the airport in Évreux without touching down.
You can follow its flight path here.
Morning opening: Another bomb alert on a European flight
An Aer Lingus flight from Dublin to Rome has been diverted to a major military base in Evreux in France after a bomb alert, the French prime minister’s office said.
The PM’s office said the government was “monitoring the situation closely.”
The flight, EIN40G, is operated by an Airbus A320. It’s currently circling above France and should start its descent to Evreux shortly.
The incident comes just two days after seven planes across Europe were searched or diverted after malicious hoax bomb alerts.
I will keep an eye on this for you.
It’s Thursday, 5 November 2026, it’s Jakub Krupa here, and this is Europe Live.
Good morning.

articles.title: India's costliest film retells a beloved Hindu epic - but divides critics
articles.summary: Easily the most anticipated Bollywood film of the year, Ramayana: Rise of a Legend is the first of two parts.

blocks.text: India's most expensive film - a lavish retelling of the Hindu epic Ramayana, made in two parts for a reported $500m - has opened in cinemas worldwide, sparking enormous expectations and mixed reviews.

Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, Ramayana: Rise of a Legend is the first of two planned films, a sprawling production that brings together some of India's biggest stars, Hollywood visual-effects expertise and two Oscar-winning composers in an attempt to take one of the country's most revered stories to a global audience.

One of Hinduism's foundational epics, the Ramayana has travelled across centuries and continents, finding expression in poetry, temple sculpture, shadow puppetry, folk theatre and stories passed down through generations. It has outlasted kingdoms and empires, inspired religious devotion and political movements, and found new life, again and again, on TV and in cinema.
Tiwari's version returns to the familiar story of love, duty, exile and war, set in a world of gods and demons, celestial weapons and mighty kingdoms.

Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Ram, the virtuous prince of Ayodhya. Banished from his kingdom for 14 years, he retreats to the forest with his wife Sita (played by Sai Pallavi), who is kidnapped by Ravana, the ten-headed king of Lanka.
Played by Yash, one of southern India's biggest stars, Ravana is a powerful warrior whose pride leads him into an epic battle with Ram (which will be depicted in part 2, set to release next year).

The film's producer, Namit Malhotra, heads visual-effects company DNEG, which has worked on Hollywood blockbusters including Dune and Interstellar. The music is a collaboration between AR Rahman, the Oscar-winning Indian composer of Slumdog Millionaire, and Hans Zimmer, whose scores for Gladiator, The Dark Knight and Dune have helped define the sound of modern Hollywood.
The film opened days ahead of Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights which celebrates Ram's return to Ayodhya after his exile.
But the response so far has been mixed.

Saibal Chatterjee of NDTV channel gave it, external three out of five stars, saying its visual spectacle often overshadowed the story. Its enormous scale, he wrote, "remains, for the most part, the only thing that stands out", while the acting remains "wildly inconsistent".
Rishabh Suri of the Hindustan Times newspaper was more enthusiastic, awarding it four stars.
"I am happy to report, all that money shows on screen," he wrote, praising the performances and visual effects, though he found the first half sluggish and the music underwhelming.

Shubhra Gupta, external of The Indian Express, who gave the film three stars, confessed to initial misgivings about its extravagant scale but found herself gradually won over, calling it the "perfect epic".
There was "enough sorcery and thrills and adventure" to sustain the spectacle, she wrote, and the filmmakers had managed to tell a sprawling story without being swallowed by it.
Internationally, too, the film drew contrasting reactions.

Writing in The Guardian, Peter Bradshaw called it a "thoroughly engaging, rousing and spectacular Indian epic melodrama". He found echoes of Shakespeare in the royal intrigue that sends Rama into exile, and of Homer in his quest to rescue Sita. Its sweeping landscapes and fantastical imagery reminded him of The Lord of the Rings and The Lion King.
"It's a rather amazing adventure," he wrote, external, giving it four stars.
Others were less impressed. Siddhant Adlakha of IGN scored the film four out of 10, describing its action as "clunky" and its computer-generated imagery as an "eye-sore".

Giovanni Lago of Next Best Picture, who gave it, external five out of 10, praised Yash's magnetic Ravana and the score by Rahman and Zimmer. But he felt the film's vast narrative might have been better served by a Game of Thrones-style series.

The use of AI to adjust actors' lip movements for the English-language version also drew criticism. While Tiwari said it was intended to make the film more accessible to international audiences, Adlakha likened the result to "exaggerated mouth movements superimposed on still images for comedy sketches".

In India, the film has invited comparisons with earlier adaptations, particularly Ramanand Sagar's Ramayan, which captivated the country nearly four decades ago with simple sets and special effects that now seem quaint.
When the series first aired in 1987, Sunday mornings across India took on an almost devotional stillness.

Streets emptied, shops lowered their shutters and neighbours crowded around TV sets. Some viewers bathed, lit incense and garlanded their screens before the broadcast, preparing for the show much as they might for worship.
Arvind Rajagopal, a media scholar at New York University, told the BBC in 2019 that trains and buses would stop and passengers disembark to watch the show on roadside TVs.

Broadcast on the state-run Doordarshan network, some of the most popular parts of the 78-episode series drew an estimated 80-100 million viewers, astonishing numbers at a time when owning a TV was a luxury in India.

The actors, too, became objects of reverence. Arun Govil, who played Ram, has recalled people weeping at the sight of him and touching his feet. Now, in a casting choice brimming with nostalgia, Govil returns in Tiwari's film as Dasharatha, Ram's father.

Other adaptations found their own ways to reimagine the epic. The 1992 Indo-Japanese animated film Ramayana: The Legend of Prince Rama brought the tale to life through richly detailed, hand-drawn animation.
Tiwari's Ramayana arrives with technological resources its predecessors could barely have imagined - but also with the expectations of generations who have grown up with the story and its characters.

It also comes at a politically charged moment in India, where Ram has become a powerful symbol of Hindu identity - over the past decade-and-a-half, even popular analyses or retellings of the epic have landed in controversy.
The 2023 film Adipurush, another big-budget retelling of Ramayana, sparked backlash on several fronts.

Hindu groups called for a ban, accusing it of disrespecting religious figures, while some critics questioned its depiction of Ravana, which they said drew on Mughal imagery and reinforced stereotypes about Muslims. The film was also criticised for its dialogue and visual effects.
For the actors portraying these characters in the latest film, that burden was deeply felt.
"I was filled with fear," Kapoor told the BBC Asian Network's Haroon Rashid. "I knew that maybe I'm too old for this. I won't be able to do justice to it."
He called the role "an opportunity of a lifetime", but said playing a figure worshipped by millions left little room for the creative freedom he had enjoyed in other films.

Sai Pallavi, who plays Sita, said the experience was as much spiritual as artistic. Raised in a religious household, she said she approached the part not just as a performance, but as an opportunity for personal growth.
The film's popular reception will become clearer soon as audiences fill cinemas.
But whatever the verdict, it marks a major cultural moment for India, bringing a story loved for generations to the big screen on an unprecedented scale.

articles.title: 1 in 3 young people in Canada have faced dating violence, pediatricians warn
articles.summary: A third of Canadian youth have faced dating violence — from physical and sexual abuse to online harassment — warns new guidance for health-care providers to help them screen for abusive relationships…

image.caption: New guidance calls on doctors to initiate conversations with young patients about healthy relationships amid an uptick in dating-related violence. (Martin Diotte/CBC)

blocks.text: Health

A third of Canadian youth have faced dating violence — from physical and sexual abuse to online harassment — warns new guidance for health-care providers to help them screen for abusive relationships among kids and teens.
New guidance calls on health-care providers to screen for relationship abuse amid uptick among kids, teens

A third of Canadian youth have faced dating violence — from physical and sexual abuse to online harassment — warns new guidance for health-care providers to help screen for abusive relationships among kids and teens.

Experiencing relationship-based violence at a young age can lead to "both immediate and long-term adverse health outcomes," notes the report, released on Thursday by the Canadian Paediatric Society (CPS). The team defined youth and teens as those in Grade 6 and up, marking the period when dating typically begins.

Health-care providers are seeing an uptick in dating-related violence, said Dr. Megan Harrison, chair of CPS's adolescent health committee, which can range from stalking to psychological abuse to sexual violence and beyond.
3rd of young Canadians aged 11 and up face dating violence, says Canadian Paediatric Society
"And part of that has to do, a little bit, with the increased use of social media and technology for teens," she said.

Violent content that's easily accessible to teens on social media — and in online pornography — is one major part of the problem, echoed Tracy Vaillancourt, a professor at the University of Ottawa and Canada Research Chair in youth mental health and violence prevention.
"It dehumanizes girls and women," she said. "And it's quite problematic to how they see relationships."
Poverty, discrimination increase risk
Multiple researchers also noted that while anyone can fall victim to violence in a romantic or sexual relationship, certain groups are at a higher risk.
Data reported by the CPS shows a higher prevalence of victims among cisgender girls and transgender and gender-diverse youth in a national sample of students in Grades 9 and 10.

items: Experts share advice for kids and teens about abusive relationships

blocks.text: Poverty, marginality and discrimination can also make some youth more vulnerable, noted Dr. Cécile Rousseau, chair of the division of child and adolescent psychiatry at McGill University.

"Sometimes this happens without any explanation, and it's hard to pinpoint why the relationship is violent and abusive, but there's also evidence to suggest that what you've endured in the past predicts what you're willing to endure in the future," Vaillancourt said.
Individuals already experiencing domestic or family violence, or kids who are bullied or rejected by their peer group, are more likely to experience violent relationships as well, she explained.
Experiencing relationship-based violence at a young age can lead to 'both immediate and long-term adverse health outcomes,' researchers said. (Ben Nelms/CBC)
'No easy answer'
So what should doctors — alongside parents and educators — watch out for?

The CPS now recommends that health-care providers, including pediatricians and primary care providers, aim to initiate conversations about healthy relationships during routine medical visits from their young patients, offer privacy and provide community resources as needed.
"Normalizing these discussions at every visit helps build rapport and provides opportunities to share knowledge with youth and caregivers," the guidance notes.

items: As 'Cornell 7' case draws attention, P.E.I. advocates call for better consent education
As more teens turn to AI for emotional support, experts say it's no substitute for human connection

blocks.text: But outside experts on dating violence questioned how much health-care providers can do to support teens properly, given the hurdles some young people face in accessing primary care in the first place, and the challenges in linking youth with long-term community support after their visit.

"Studies of adults show that screening for intimate partner violence is only a good thing if you also have resources," Vaillancourt added. "So asking somebody if they're in an unsafe situation and then doing nothing about it is actually quite problematic."

items: Organized crime is using encrypted messaging apps to enlist youth. This spells trouble for police
B.C. Chamber of Commerce delegates reject call for social media, AI ban for kids

blocks.text: Rousseau, from McGill University, said while health-care providers play a "key role" in tackling youth violence, they face an uphill battle given the complexities around why modern teens end up being victims of abuse — or turn to violence themselves.

"Teen dating violence is a problem, but also self-harm, suicide … all of that is increasing very rapidly," said Rousseau, who added the rapid shifts in how teens use technology make it hard for researchers to keep up.
"There is no easy answer," she said.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Lauren Pelley is a senior health and medical reporter for CBC News. She's a two-time RNAO Media Award winner for in-depth health reporting in 2020 and 2022, a silver medallist for best editorial newsletter at the 2024 Digital Publishing Awards, and a 2024 Covering Climate Now award winner in the health category. Contact her at: lauren.pelley@cbc.ca.
